newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania police halt rallies, opponents scan moves.
newsitem.headline: Albania police halt rallies, opponents scan moves.

text.p: Police chased protesters away from rallies denouncing Albanian President Sali Berisha over the demise of popular investment schemes, prompting his opponents to reconsider their strategy against his government.
Police prevented a banned demonstration being held in Tirana's Skanderbeg Square on Saturday by using batons against protesters, journalists and anyone else caught in their path.
Similar action in the southern town of Fier cleared a crowd of 2,000 demanding the return of their lost savings.
But 40,000 marchers poured unimpeded through the streets of the port of Vlore in a fourth consecutive day of rallies and promised to return on Sunday.
The Forum For Democracy opposition grouping said 15 of its leaders were briefly detained by Tirana police. One activist, a large purple welt covering his forehead, said he had been severely beaten.
The opposition admitted that the failure of its rallies in the capital for a second weekend handicapped its "Flowers not Stones" campaign against the rightist government.
"The country's economic situation is simply catastrophic," Fatos Lubonja, a Forum leader and former political prisoner under Albania's hardline communists, told a news conference.
"Our strategy can involve only peaceful means. We hope one day soon there will be the chance for dialogue."
The Forum said it would announce new measures on Sunday. Its leaders blame Berisha for the collapse of the pyramid investment schemes.
They seek the creation of a "technocrat government" to usher in market reforms. But many admit they have little command of economics.
State television, reviled by the opposition, said merely that the Tirana rally, banned by the Interior Ministry on safety grounds, had not taken place.
It aired government statements denying that oppostion leaders had been rounded up or beaten. It said journalists had been attacked by "angry protesters" and called for them to be given protection.

Three men identifying themselves as members of "special sescurity forces" pushed their way into Reuters Tirana office on Saturday and demanded pictures and television film of the abortive rally. They left without incident.
Berisha issued a statement denouncing all violence associated with the protests. But he added that failure to obey the law could push the situation beyond the control of police.
He has failed to appear in public since talks on the crisis last Tuesday, boycotted by the Forum on the grounds that some of its activists remained in jail after widespread disturbances last month.
Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, who also heads the ruling Democratic Party, has proposed fresh talks next week.

The government started handing out partial refunds to investors in two failed schemes last week. But fresh protests erupted in Vlore after a locally-based fund, which owed some $500 million, caved in.
Economists suggest there could soon be new failures among the schemes, which attracted funds from virtually every family in Albania with promises of high regular interest payments.

The Democrats won re-election last year in polls criticised as unfair by Western observers. Some opposition politicians accuse the party of financing its victory with proceeds from the failed pyramid companies.
